Basic data handling: SetDifference.name: Basic data handling: SetDifference
Basic data handling: SetDifference.description:
Returns the difference between two SETs.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns a new SET containing
elements in the first SET but not in the second SET.
output_tooltips: Elements in set1 that are not in set2.

item.tooltip: The item to remove if present.

Basic data handling: SetDiscard.name: Basic data handling: SetDiscard
Basic data handling: SetDiscard.description:
Removes an item from a SET if it is present.

This node takes a SET and any item as inputs, then returns a new SET
with the item removed. Unlike remove, no error is raised if the item is not present.
output_tooltips: The SET with the item removed (unchanged when it was absent).

start.tooltip: Index value assigned to the first element.

Basic data handling: SetEnumerate.name: Basic data handling: SetEnumerate
Basic data handling: SetEnumerate.description:
Enumerates elements in a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns a LIST of tuples where each tuple
contains an index and a value from the SET. The start parameter specifies the
initial index value (default is 0).

Note: Since SETs are unordered, the enumeration order is arbitrary but consistent
within a single operation.
output_tooltips: List of (index, value) pairs. Order is arbitrary but stable within one operation.

Basic data handling: SetIntersection.name: Basic data handling: SetIntersection
Basic data handling: SetIntersection.description:
Returns the intersection of two or more SETs.

This node takes multiple SETs as input and returns a new SET containing
only elements present in all input SETs.
output_tooltips: Elements present in all of the input SETs.

Basic data handling: SetIsDisjoint.name: Basic data handling: SetIsDisjoint
Basic data handling: SetIsDisjoint.description:
Checks if two SETs have no elements in common.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns True if they have no elements in common.
output_tooltips: True when the two SETs share no elements.

set2.tooltip: SET that may contain all of set1's elements.

Basic data handling: SetIsSubset.name: Basic data handling: SetIsSubset
Basic data handling: SetIsSubset.description:
Checks if set1 is a subset of set2.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns True if set1 is a subset of set2
(all elements in set1 are also in set2).
output_tooltips: True when every element of set1 is also in set2.

set2.tooltip: SET whose elements must all be in set1.

Basic data handling: SetIsSuperset.name: Basic data handling: SetIsSuperset
Basic data handling: SetIsSuperset.description:
Checks if set1 is a superset of set2.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns True if set1 is a superset of set2
(set1 contains all elements in set2).
output_tooltips: True when set1 contains every element of set2.

Basic data handling: SetLength.name: Basic data handling: SetLength
Basic data handling: SetLength.description:
Returns the number of items in a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns its length (number of elements) as an integer.
output_tooltips: The number of elements in the SET.

set.tooltip: The SET to pop an item from.

Basic data handling: SetPop.name: Basic data handling: SetPop
Basic data handling: SetPop.description:
Removes and returns an arbitrary item from a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns both the new SET
with an arbitrary item removed and the removed item.
When the SET is empty, the item is None.
output_tooltips: The SET with an arbitrary item removed.
The removed item (None when the SET was empty).

set.tooltip: The SET to pop a random element from.

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible selection. Leave empty to pick randomly each run.

Basic data handling: SetPopRandom.name: Basic data handling: SetPopRandom
Basic data handling: SetPopRandom.description:
Removes and returns a random element from a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns the SET with a random element removed
and the removed element itself. If the SET is empty, it returns None for the element.
An optional seed can be provided for reproducible selection.
output_tooltips: The SET with a random element removed.
The removed element (None when the SET was empty).

Basic data handling: SetRemove.name: Basic data handling: SetRemove
Basic data handling: SetRemove.description:
Removes an item from a SET.

This node takes a SET and any item as inputs, then returns a new SET
with the item removed and a success indicator. If the item is not present,
the original SET is returned with success set to False.
output_tooltips: The SET with the item removed.
True when the item was present and removed.

set.tooltip: The SET of numbers to sum.

start.tooltip: Initial value added to the sum.

Basic data handling: SetSum.name: Basic data handling: SetSum
Basic data handling: SetSum.description:
Calculates the sum of all elements in a SET.

This node takes a SET as input and returns the sum of all its elements.
The optional start parameter specifies the initial value (default is 0).

Note: This operation requires all elements to be numeric or otherwise
compatible with addition. If the SET contains mixed or incompatible types,
it may raise an error.
output_tooltips: The total as an integer.
The total as a float.

Basic data handling: SetSymmetricDiffere.name: Basic data handling: SetSymmetricDifference
Basic data handling: SetSymmetricDiffere.description:
Returns the symmetric difference between two SETs.

This node takes two SETs as input and returns a new SET containing
elements in either SET but not in both.
output_tooltips: Elements present in exactly one of the two SETs.

Basic data handling: SetUnion.name: Basic data handling: SetUnion
Basic data handling: SetUnion.description:
Returns the union of two or more SETs.

This node takes multiple SETs as input and returns a new SET containing
all elements from all the input SETs.
output_tooltips: All elements from every input SET (duplicates removed).

Basic data handling: SetToDataList.name: Basic data handling: SetToDataList
Basic data handling: SetToDataList.description:
Converts a SET object into a ComfyUI data list.

This node takes a SET object (Python set as a single variable) and
converts it to a ComfyUI data list, allowing its items to be processed
individually by nodes that accept data lists.
output_tooltips: The SET's elements as a ComfyUI data list.

Basic data handling: SetToList.name: Basic data handling: SetToList
Basic data handling: SetToList.description:
Converts a SET into a LIST.

This node takes a SET input and creates a new LIST containing all elements
from the SET. Note that the order of elements in the resulting LIST is arbitrary
since SETs are unordered collections.
output_tooltips: The SET's elements as a Python LIST (order is arbitrary).

value.tooltip: The number to take the absolute value of.

Basic data handling: MathAbs.name: Basic data handling: MathAbs
Basic data handling: MathAbs.description:
Returns the absolute value of a number.

This node takes a number and returns its absolute value (magnitude without sign).
output_tooltips: The absolute (non-negative) value of the input.

value.tooltip: The value (in [-1, 1]) whose arc cosine is computed.

Basic data handling: MathAcos.name: Basic data handling: MathAcos
Basic data handling: MathAcos.description:
Calculates the arc cosine (inverse cosine) of a value.

This node takes a value between -1 and 1, and returns the arc cosine in radians or degrees.
The arc cosine is the inverse operation of cosine, returning the angle whose cosine is the input value.
output_tooltips: The arc cosine angle in the chosen unit.

value.tooltip: The value (in [-1, 1]) whose arc sine is computed.

Basic data handling: MathAsin.name: Basic data handling: MathAsin
Basic data handling: MathAsin.description:
Calculates the arc sine (inverse sine) of a value.

This node takes a value between -1 and 1, and returns the arc sine in radians or degrees.
The arc sine is the inverse operation of sine, returning the angle whose sine is the input value.
output_tooltips: The arc sine angle in the chosen unit.

value.tooltip: The value whose arc tangent is computed.

Basic data handling: MathAtan.name: Basic data handling: MathAtan
Basic data handling: MathAtan.description:
Calculates the arc tangent (inverse tangent) of a value.

This node takes a value and returns the arc tangent in radians or degrees.
The arc tangent is the inverse operation of tangent, returning the angle whose tangent is the input value.
output_tooltips: The arc tangent angle in the chosen unit.

Basic data handling: MathAtan2.name: Basic data handling: MathAtan2
Basic data handling: MathAtan2.description:
Calculates the arc tangent of y/x, considering the quadrant.

This node takes y and x coordinates and returns the arc tangent in radians or degrees.
Unlike atan(y/x), this function handles the case where x is zero and correctly determines
the quadrant of the resulting angle.
output_tooltips: The angle of the point (x, y) in the chosen unit.

value.tooltip: The number to round up.

Basic data handling: MathCeil.name: Basic data handling: MathCeil
Basic data handling: MathCeil.description:
Returns the ceiling of a number.

This node takes a number and returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the input value.
output_tooltips: The smallest integer greater than or equal to the value.

angle.tooltip: The angle to take the cosine of.

Basic data handling: MathCos.name: Basic data handling: MathCos
Basic data handling: MathCos.description:
Calculates the cosine of an angle in radians or degrees.

This node takes an angle value and unit type, and returns the cosine of that angle.
The cosine of an angle is the ratio of the length of the adjacent side to the length
of the hypotenuse in a right-angled triangle.
output_tooltips: The cosine of the angle.

radians.tooltip: The angle in radians to convert.

Basic data handling: MathDegrees.name: Basic data handling: MathDegrees
Basic data handling: MathDegrees.description:
Converts an angle from radians to degrees.

This node takes an angle in radians and returns the equivalent angle in degrees.
output_tooltips: The equivalent angle in degrees.

Basic data handling: MathE.name: Basic data handling: MathE
Basic data handling: MathE.description:
Returns the mathematical constant e.

This node returns the value of e (Euler's number), which is approximately 2.71828.
output_tooltips: Euler's number e, approximately 2.71828.

value.tooltip: The exponent x in e^x.

Basic data handling: MathExp.name: Basic data handling: MathExp
Basic data handling: MathExp.description:
Calculates the exponential of a number (e^x).

This node takes a number and returns e (Euler's number) raised to the power of that number.
output_tooltips: e raised to the power of the input value.

value.tooltip: The number to round down.

Basic data handling: MathFloor.name: Basic data handling: MathFloor
Basic data handling: MathFloor.description:
Returns the floor of a number.

This node takes a number and returns the largest integer less than or equal to the input value.
output_tooltips: The largest integer less than or equal to the value.

value.tooltip: The positive number to take the logarithm of.

base.tooltip: Logarithm base; e gives the natural logarithm.

Basic data handling: MathLog.name: Basic data handling: MathLog
Basic data handling: MathLog.description:
Calculates the natural logarithm (base e) of a number.

This node takes a positive number and returns its natural logarithm.
If the specified base is not 'e', calculates the logarithm with the specified base.
output_tooltips: The logarithm of the value in the chosen base.

value.tooltip: The positive number to take the base-10 logarithm of.

Basic data handling: MathLog10.name: Basic data handling: MathLog10
Basic data handling: MathLog10.description:
Calculates the base-10 logarithm of a number.

This node takes a positive number and returns its base-10 logarithm.
output_tooltips: The base-10 logarithm of the value.

Basic data handling: MathMax.name: Basic data handling: MathMax
Basic data handling: MathMax.description:
Returns the maximum value among the inputs.

This node takes two or more values and returns the maximum value among them.
The function works with both FLOAT and INT types.
output_tooltips: The larger of the two input values.

Basic data handling: MathMin.name: Basic data handling: MathMin
Basic data handling: MathMin.description:
Returns the minimum value among the inputs.

This node takes two or more values and returns the minimum value among them.
The function works with both FLOAT and INT types.
output_tooltips: The smaller of the two input values.

Basic data handling: MathPi.name: Basic data handling: MathPi
Basic data handling: MathPi.description:
Returns the mathematical constant π (pi).

This node returns the value of π, which is approximately 3.14159.
output_tooltips: The mathematical constant pi, approximately 3.14159.

degrees.tooltip: The angle in degrees to convert.

Basic data handling: MathRadians.name: Basic data handling: MathRadians
Basic data handling: MathRadians.description:
Converts an angle from degrees to radians.

This node takes an angle in degrees and returns the equivalent angle in radians.
output_tooltips: The equivalent angle in radians.

angle.tooltip: The angle to take the sine of.

Basic data handling: MathSin.name: Basic data handling: MathSin
Basic data handling: MathSin.description:
Calculates the sine of an angle in radians or degrees.

This node takes an angle value and unit type, and returns the sine of that angle.
The sine of an angle is the ratio of the length of the opposite side to the length
of the hypotenuse in a right-angled triangle.
output_tooltips: The sine of the angle.

value.tooltip: The non-negative number to take the square root of.

Basic data handling: MathSqrt.name: Basic data handling: MathSqrt
Basic data handling: MathSqrt.description:
Calculates the square root of a non-negative number.

This node takes a non-negative number and returns its square root.
output_tooltips: The square root of the value.

angle.tooltip: The angle to take the tangent of.

Basic data handling: MathTan.name: Basic data handling: MathTan
Basic data handling: MathTan.description:
Calculates the tangent of an angle in radians or degrees.

This node takes an angle value and unit type, and returns the tangent of that angle.
The tangent of an angle is the ratio of the length of the opposite side to the length
of the adjacent side in a right-angled triangle.
output_tooltips: The tangent of the angle (raises an error where the tangent is undefined).

formula.tooltip: Expression to evaluate using single-letter variables (a, b, c, ...), supported operators, parentheses and functions. Example: sqrt(a**2 + b**2).

a.tooltip: A numeric value bound to a single-letter variable in the formula. Connect more values to add the variables b, c, d, ...

Basic data handling: MathFormula.name: Basic data handling: MathFormula
Basic data handling: MathFormula.description:
A node that evaluates a mathematical formula provided as a string without using eval.

This node takes an arbitrary number of numerical inputs (single letters like `a`, `b`, `c`, etc.) and safely
evaluates the formula with supported operations: +, -, *, /, //, %, **, parentheses, and mathematical
functions.

NOTE on Operator Precedence: This parser uses standard precedence rules. Unary minus binds tightly,
so expressions like `-a ** 2` are interpreted as `(-a) ** 2`. To calculate `-(a ** 2)`,
use parentheses: `-(a ** 2)`.

The identifiers `e` and `pi` are special. When used as a function call (`e()`, `pi()`), they return their
respective mathematical constants. When used as a variable (`e`), they expect a corresponding input.

Supported functions:
- Basic: abs, floor, ceil, round, min(a,b), max(a,b)
- Trigonometric: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2(y,x), degrees, radians
- Hyperbolic: sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh
- Exponential & Logarithmic: exp, log, log10, log2, sqrt, pow(base,exp)
- Constants (must be called with empty parentheses): pi(), e()
output_tooltips: The numerical result of evaluating the formula.

Basic data handling: StringCapitalize.name: Basic data handling: StringCapitalize
Basic data handling: StringCapitalize.description: Converts the first character of the input string to uppercase and all other characters to lowercase.
output_tooltips: The text with its first character uppercased and the rest lowercased.

Basic data handling: StringCasefold.name: Basic data handling: StringCasefold
Basic data handling: StringCasefold.description:
Converts text to lowercase in a way optimized for case-insensitive comparisons.

This node is especially useful when comparing text that might contain special characters.
Unlike standard lowercase, this handles special cases like converting the German 'ß' to "ss".
Use this node when you need the most accurate case-insensitive text matching.
output_tooltips: The text casefolded for case-insensitive comparisons.

width.tooltip: Total width of the resulting field.

fillchar.tooltip: Padding character (only its first character is used).

Basic data handling: StringCenter.name: Basic data handling: StringCenter
Basic data handling: StringCenter.description:
Centers text within a specified width.

This node takes a string and centers it within a field of the specified width.
By default, it uses spaces as padding characters, but you can specify any
single character to use as padding.
output_tooltips: The text centered within the field width.

Basic data handling: StringConcat.name: Basic data handling: StringConcat
Basic data handling: StringConcat.description: Combines two text strings together, joining them end-to-end.
output_tooltips: The two texts joined end-to-end.

substring.tooltip: The text whose occurrences are counted.

start.tooltip: Start position of the search range.

end.tooltip: End position of the search range (0 means the end).

Basic data handling: StringCount.name: Basic data handling: StringCount
Basic data handling: StringCount.description:
Counts occurrences of a substring within a string.

This node returns the number of times the specified substring appears in the input string.
You can optionally specify start and end positions to limit the search range.
output_tooltips: The number of non-overlapping occurrences of the substring.

bytes_string.tooltip: String representation of bytes, e.g. b'text', as produced by the encode node.

Basic data handling: StringDecode.name: Basic data handling: StringDecode
Basic data handling: StringDecode.description:
Converts a bytes-like string representation back to a text string.

This node takes a string representation of bytes (like those produced by the StringEncode node)
and converts it back to a regular text string using the specified encoding.
Useful for processing encoded data received from files or network sources.
output_tooltips: The decoded text (or an error message when decoding fails).

errors.tooltip: How to handle characters that cannot be encoded.

Basic data handling: StringEncode.name: Basic data handling: StringEncode
Basic data handling: StringEncode.description:
Converts a string to bytes using the specified encoding.

This node encodes text using different character encodings like UTF-8 (default),
ASCII, or others. It's useful for preparing text for file saving or
network transmission in specific formats.
output_tooltips: The bytes as a string representation (or an error message on failure).

start.tooltip: Start position of the checked range.

end.tooltip: End position of the checked range (0 means the end).

Basic data handling: StringEndswith.name: Basic data handling: StringEndswith
Basic data handling: StringEndswith.description:
Checks if a string ends with the specified suffix.

This node tests whether the input string ends with a particular substring.
Returns True if the string ends with the specified suffix, otherwise False.
Optional start and end parameters allow you to check only a specific portion of the string.
output_tooltips: True when the text ends with the suffix.

Basic data handling: StringEscape.name: Basic data handling: StringEscape
Basic data handling: StringEscape.description:
Escapes a string by converting special characters to escape sequences.

    This node converts characters like newlines, tabs, quotes, and backslashes to their escaped
    representation (like '
', '    ', '"', '\'). Useful when you need to prepare strings
    for formats that require escaped sequences instead of literal special characters.
output_tooltips: The text with special characters turned into escape sequences.

tabsize.tooltip: Number of spaces each tab expands to.

Basic data handling: StringExpandtabs.name: Basic data handling: StringExpandtabs
Basic data handling: StringExpandtabs.description:
Replaces tab characters with spaces.

This node replaces all tab characters ('    ') in a string with spaces.
The tab size (number of spaces per tab) can be adjusted,
with a default value of 8 characters.
output_tooltips: The text with tab characters replaced by spaces.

start.tooltip: Start position of the search range.

end.tooltip: End position of the search range (0 means the end).

Basic data handling: StringFind.name: Basic data handling: StringFind
Basic data handling: StringFind.description:
Finds the first occurrence of a substring in a string.

This node searches for the first occurrence of the specified substring within the input string.
Returns the lowest index where the substring is found. If the substring is not found, it returns -1.
Optional start and end parameters allow you to limit the search to a specific portion of the string.
output_tooltips: Index of the first occurrence, or -1 when not found.

template.tooltip: Format string with {placeholder} fields referencing mapping keys.

mapping.tooltip: Dictionary providing the values for the placeholders.

Basic data handling: StringFormatMap.name: Basic data handling: StringFormatMap
Basic data handling: StringFormatMap.description:
Formats a string using values from a dictionary.

This node replaces placeholders in the input string with values from a dictionary.
It uses the same placeholder syntax as the format() method, but takes the values from a dictionary
mapping keys to values. For example, the string "Hello, {name}" with a dictionary {"name": "World"}
would produce "Hello, World".
output_tooltips: The formatted string (or an error message when a key is missing).

Basic data handling: StringIn.name: Basic data handling: StringIn
Basic data handling: StringIn.description:
Checks if a string contains a specified substring.

This node implements the 'in' operator for strings. It checks whether the given substring
exists within the input string. Returns True if the substring is found,
otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when the substring occurs in the text.

Basic data handling: StringIsAlnum.name: Basic data handling: StringIsAlnum
Basic data handling: StringIsAlnum.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are alphanumeric.

This node returns True if all characters in the string are alphanumeric
(letters or numbers) and there is at least one character, otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when all characters are alphanumeric and the string is non-empty.

Basic data handling: StringIsAlpha.name: Basic data handling: StringIsAlpha
Basic data handling: StringIsAlpha.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are alphabetic.

This node returns True if all characters in the string are alphabetic
(letters) and there is at least one character, otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when all characters are alphabetic and the string is non-empty.

Basic data handling: StringIsAscii.name: Basic data handling: StringIsAscii
Basic data handling: StringIsAscii.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are ASCII characters.

This node returns True if all characters in the string are in the ASCII character
set and there is at least one character, otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when every character is in the ASCII character set.

Basic data handling: StringIsDecimal.name: Basic data handling: StringIsDecimal
Basic data handling: StringIsDecimal.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are decimal characters.

This node returns True if all characters in the string are decimal
characters and there is at least one character, otherwise False.
Decimal characters include digit characters and characters that can be
used to form decimal numbers in various locales.
output_tooltips: True when all characters are decimal digits and the string is non-empty.

Basic data handling: StringIsDigit.name: Basic data handling: StringIsDigit
Basic data handling: StringIsDigit.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are digits.

This node returns True if all characters in the string are digits
and there is at least one character, otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when all characters are digits and the string is non-empty.

Basic data handling: StringIsIdentifier.name: Basic data handling: StringIsIdentifier
Basic data handling: StringIsIdentifier.description:
Checks if the string is a valid identifier in Python.

This node returns True if the string is a valid Python identifier,
otherwise False. A valid identifier must start with a letter or underscore
and can only contain letters, digits, or underscores.
output_tooltips: True when the string is a valid Python identifier.

Basic data handling: StringIsLower.name: Basic data handling: StringIsLower
Basic data handling: StringIsLower.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are lowercase.

This node returns True if all cased characters in the string are lowercase
and there is at least one cased character, otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when all cased characters are lowercase and at least one exists.

Basic data handling: StringIsNumeric.name: Basic data handling: StringIsNumeric
Basic data handling: StringIsNumeric.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are numeric.

This node returns True if all characters in the string are numeric
and there is at least one character, otherwise False. Numeric characters include
digit characters and characters that have the Unicode numeric value property.
output_tooltips: True when all characters are numeric and the string is non-empty.

Basic data handling: StringIsPrintable.name: Basic data handling: StringIsPrintable
Basic data handling: StringIsPrintable.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are printable.

This node returns True if all characters in the string are printable or the string is empty,
otherwise False. Printable characters are those which are not control characters.
output_tooltips: True when all characters are printable.

Basic data handling: StringIsSpace.name: Basic data handling: StringIsSpace
Basic data handling: StringIsSpace.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are whitespace.

This node returns True if all characters in the string are whitespace
and there is at least one character, otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when all characters are whitespace and the string is non-empty.

Basic data handling: StringIsTitle.name: Basic data handling: StringIsTitle
Basic data handling: StringIsTitle.description:
Checks if the string is titlecased.

This node returns True if the string is titlecased and there is at least one
character, otherwise False. A titlecased string has all words start with an
uppercase character and continue with lowercase.
output_tooltips: True when the string is titlecased.

Basic data handling: StringIsUpper.name: Basic data handling: StringIsUpper
Basic data handling: StringIsUpper.description:
Checks if all characters in the string are uppercase.

This node returns True if all cased characters in the string are uppercase
and there is at least one cased character, otherwise False.
output_tooltips: True when all cased characters are uppercase and at least one exists.

Basic data handling: StringLength.name: Basic data handling: StringLength
Basic data handling: StringLength.description:
Returns the length of a string.

This node calculates and returns the number of characters in the input string.
It works the same way as Python's built-in len() function for strings.
output_tooltips: The number of characters in the text.

strings.tooltip: Data list of strings to join.

sep.tooltip: Separator placed between each pair of strings.

Basic data handling: StringDataListJoin.name: Basic data handling: StringDataListJoin
Basic data handling: StringDataListJoin.description:
Joins strings from a data list with a specified separator.

This node takes a data list of strings and concatenates them, with the specified
separator string between each element. The separator is inserted between the strings,
not at the beginning or end of the result.
output_tooltips: The strings joined with the separator.

sep.tooltip: Separator placed between each pair of strings.

Basic data handling: StringListJoin.name: Basic data handling: StringListJoin
Basic data handling: StringListJoin.description:
Joins strings from a LIST with a specified separator.

This node takes a data list of strings and concatenates them, with the specified
separator string between each element. The separator is inserted between the strings,
not at the beginning or end of the result.
output_tooltips: The strings joined with the separator.

width.tooltip: Total width of the resulting field.

fillchar.tooltip: Padding character (only its first character is used).

Basic data handling: StringLjust.name: Basic data handling: StringLjust
Basic data handling: StringLjust.description:
Left-aligns the string within a field of a given width.

This node returns a string left-aligned in a field of the specified width.
If fillchar is provided, it is used as the padding character instead of a space.
output_tooltips: The text left-aligned within the field width.

Basic data handling: StringLower.name: Basic data handling: StringLower
Basic data handling: StringLower.description:
Converts the string to lowercase.

This node returns a copy of the string with all uppercase characters converted to lowercase.
output_tooltips: The text converted to lowercase.

chars.tooltip: Set of characters to remove from the start (whitespace when empty).

Basic data handling: StringLstrip.name: Basic data handling: StringLstrip
Basic data handling: StringLstrip.description:
Removes leading characters from the string.

This node returns a copy of the string with leading characters removed.
If chars is provided, it specifies the set of characters to be removed.
If chars is not provided, whitespace characters are removed.
output_tooltips: The text with leading characters removed.

prefix.tooltip: The prefix to remove when present.

Basic data handling: StringRemoveprefix.name: Basic data handling: StringRemoveprefix
Basic data handling: StringRemoveprefix.description:
Removes prefix from the string if present.

This node returns a copy of the string with the specified prefix removed
if the string starts with that prefix, otherwise returns the original string.
output_tooltips: The text without the prefix (unchanged when the prefix is absent).

suffix.tooltip: The suffix to remove when present.

Basic data handling: StringRemovesuffix.name: Basic data handling: StringRemovesuffix
Basic data handling: StringRemovesuffix.description:
Removes suffix from the string if present.

This node returns a copy of the string with the specified suffix removed
if the string ends with that suffix, otherwise returns the original string.
output_tooltips: The text without the suffix (unchanged when the suffix is absent).

count.tooltip: Maximum number of replacements (-1 replaces all).

Basic data handling: StringReplace.name: Basic data handling: StringReplace
Basic data handling: StringReplace.description:
Replaces occurrences of a substring with another substring.

This node returns a copy of the string with all occurrences of substring
old replaced by new. If the optional argument count is given, only the

bit_depth.tooltip: WAV encoding. 24-bit PCM is the default; 32-bit float can preserve over-full-scale samples when normalization is disabled.

overwrite.tooltip: If enabled, existing files will be overwritten. If disabled, a numbered suffix is added.

normalize_clipping.tooltip: If enabled, peak-normalizes clipped audio. If disabled, 24-bit PCM hard-clips to -1 dBFS while 32-bit float saves over-full-scale samples.

SaveAudioWithPath.name: SaveAudioWithPath
SaveAudioWithPath.description: Saves audio to a specified folder with a subfolder as an uncompressed WAV file.

remove_extension.tooltip: Remove file extension from output name

frames_limit.tooltip: Maximum number of output frames. Use -1 to load the complete video.

framerate.tooltip: -1 keeps the source rate. Lower values retain evenly spaced frames; values above the source rate keep the source rate.

even_batch_picker.tooltip: After Frames limit, retain this many frames evenly across that range using the same selection as Even Batch Picker (CRT). -1 or 0 keeps the complete limited range.

megapixels.tooltip: After even-frame selection, resize only the retained frames to this target area with Lanczos while preserving aspect ratio.

folder_path.tooltip: Base folder path to save the file

subfolder_name.tooltip: Subfolder name within the base folder

filename.tooltip: File name (without extension). Leave empty to number files incrementally starting at 0.

overwrite.tooltip: If enabled, existing files will be overwritten. If disabled, a numbered suffix like _001 is added.

SaveLatentsConditioning.name: SaveLatentsConditioning
SaveLatentsConditioning.description: Saves a latent and a conditioning together in a single .safetensors file. Load them back with 'Load Latents Conditioning (CRT)'.

LoadLatentsConditioning.name: LoadLatentsConditioning
LoadLatentsConditioning.description: Loads a latent + conditioning pair saved with 'Save Latents Conditioning (CRT)', selected by seed. If an audio file with the same name sits next to the .safetensors file, it is returned on the 'audio' output (None when no matching audio exists).

prompt.default: A beautiful landscape...

CRT_AddSettingsAndPrompt.name: CRT_AddSettingsAndPrompt
CRT_AddSettingsAndPrompt.description:
Adds a text block with settings and a prompt to an image,
either horizontally at the bottom or vertically on the right.
The block's size is dynamically adjusted to fit the text.
Fonts are loaded from: ComfyUI/custom_nodes/CRT-Nodes/Fonts

batch_count.tooltip: Number of items to generate with different seeds. Higher values = more VRAM in parallel mode.

model_high_noise.tooltip: Model used for the initial high-noise denoising phase. Typically handles structure and composition.

model_low_noise.tooltip: Model used for the final low-noise refinement phase. Typically handles details and fine features.

positive.tooltip: Positive prompt conditioning. Describes what you want to generate.

width.tooltip: Output width in pixels. Will be quantized to nearest multiple of 16.

height.tooltip: Output height in pixels. Will be quantized to nearest multiple of 16.

frame_count.tooltip: Number of frames to generate. Use 1 for images, >1 for videos.

seed.tooltip: Starting seed for generation. Each batch item uses seed+N if increment is enabled.

increment_seed.tooltip: If enabled, each batch item gets seed+1, seed+2, etc. If disabled, all use the same seed.

steps.tooltip: Total number of denoising steps. More steps = better quality but slower generation.

boundary.tooltip: Sigma value where switching from high-noise to low-noise model occurs. Lower = earlier switch.

sigma_shift.tooltip: Shifts the noise schedule. Higher values = more denoising emphasis on high-frequency details.

cfg_high_noise.tooltip: Classifier-Free Guidance scale for high-noise phase. Higher = stronger prompt adherence.

cfg_low_noise.tooltip: Classifier-Free Guidance scale for low-noise phase. Higher = stronger prompt adherence.

sampler_name.tooltip: Sampling algorithm. Different samplers have different quality/speed tradeoffs.

scheduler.tooltip: Noise schedule that controls how denoising steps are distributed.

enable_vae_decode.tooltip: Decode latents to images. Disable to only output latents.

create_comparison_grid.tooltip: Create a side-by-side comparison grid of all batch outputs.

save_videos_images.tooltip: Save outputs to disk. Disable to only use outputs in workflow.

save_folder_path.tooltip: Root folder where outputs will be saved.

save_subfolder_name.tooltip: Subfolder name inside the root folder for organizing outputs.

save_filename_prefix.tooltip: Prefix for output filenames. Seed will be appended automatically.

fps.tooltip: Frames per second for video outputs. Only relevant when frame_count > 1.

processing_mode.tooltip: Parallel = process all batches together (fast, high VRAM). Sequential = one at a time (slow, low VRAM).

offload_conditioning.tooltip: Offload text conditioning to CPU between items. Reduces VRAM slightly, forces sequential mode.

negative.tooltip: Optional negative conditioning. If disconnected, empty negative conditioning is auto-generated from positive.

vae.tooltip: VAE model for encoding/decoding. Required if enable_vae_decode is True or using I2V mode.

start_image.tooltip: Starting image for Image-to-Video generation. When provided, switches to I2V mode automatically.

Batch Randomize.tooltip: Shuffle without repeats across incrementing seeds. Every file is presented once before a new shuffled cycle begins. No cache is stored. Disabled keeps consecutive selection.

weighted_phrases.tooltip: Shared KREA2 weights applied to every selected prompt. Use (phrase:-1) to suppress or (phrase:1.5) to emphasize. The phrase must occur in the prompt.

strength.tooltip: Global multiplier for the shared weighting effect. Use sampler CFG 1.0 with KREA2.

Batch Randomize.tooltip: Shuffle without repeats across incrementing seeds. Every file is presented before a new cycle begins.

CRT_FileBatchPromptSchedulerKREA2.name: CRT_FileBatchPromptSchedulerKREA2
CRT_FileBatchPromptSchedulerKREA2.description: Loads a scheduled batch of prompt files, applies one shared set of KREA2 phrase weights to the whole batch, and returns the patched model. Use CFG 1.0.

folder_path.tooltip: Path to the folder containing the text files

batch_count.tooltip: Number of files to load in the batch

seed.tooltip: Acts as a batch offset. Set to 0 to start from the first file.

file_extension.tooltip: The file extension to filter for (e.g., .txt)

max_words.tooltip: Maximum number of words per output (0 for no limit)

crawl_subfolders.tooltip: Whether to include files in subfolders

max_side_length.tooltip: The absolute maximum size (in pixels) for either the width or height of the final image.

consolidate_lines.tooltip: If True, removes line breaks within each individual string input

join_with.tooltip: 'Newline' for 'return to line' behavior between strings

suffix.tooltip: Character(s) to add to the end of each string before joining

save_to_file.tooltip: Enable to save each processed string as a .txt file

file_path.tooltip: The directory within the main output folder to save the .txt files to

filename_prefix.tooltip: The prefix for the saved filenames

split_symbol.tooltip: A custom character or string to split by. If empty, splits by empty lines.

strip_whitespace.tooltip: Remove leading/trailing whitespace from each split part

increment_seed.tooltip: If enabled, each batch item gets seed+1, seed+2, etc. If disabled, all items use the same seed.

image_megapixels.tooltip: Target resolution in megapixels. Images are resized (lanczos) preserving aspect ratio and quantized to VAE boundaries before encoding.

edit_model_flux2klein.tooltip: Enable ReferenceLatent-style conditioning for edit/fill models (flux2klein). Forces denoise=1 and samples from an empty latent. Requires image input.

reference_mode.tooltip: per_item: each image in the batch is used as its own reference latent. shared: image[0] is used as the reference for every batch item.

enable_vae_decode.tooltip: Decode latents to images using the VAE.

create_comparison_grid.tooltip: Create a horizontal side-by-side comparison grid of all batch outputs.

save_folder_path.tooltip: Root folder where outputs will be saved.

save_subfolder_name.tooltip: Subfolder inside the root folder for organizing outputs.

save_filename_prefix.tooltip: Prefix for output filenames. Seed is appended automatically.

latent_image.tooltip: Starting latent. If image is also connected, image takes priority. If neither input is connected, a dummy empty latent is auto-generated using VAE channel info.

image.tooltip: Input image batch. Resized to image_megapixels before encoding. In normal mode: VAE-encoded as the starting latent. In edit_model_flux2klein mode: used as reference latent; sampling starts from an empty latent.

increment_seed.tooltip: Each batch item gets seed+1, seed+2, etc. Disable to use same seed for all.

image_megapixels.tooltip: Target resolution in megapixels. Images are resized (lanczos) preserving aspect ratio.

edit_model_flux2klein.tooltip: Enable ReferenceLatent-style conditioning for edit/fill models (flux2klein).

reference_mode.tooltip: per_item: each image is its own reference. shared: image[0] is reference for all.

enable_vae_decode.tooltip: Decode latents to images using the VAE.

create_comparison_grid.tooltip: Create a horizontal side-by-side comparison grid.

latent_image.tooltip: Starting latent. If image is also connected, image takes priority. If neither is connected, a dummy empty latent is auto-generated.

image.tooltip: Input image batch. Resized to image_megapixels before encoding. In edit_model_flux2klein mode: used as reference latent.

text.tooltip: Displays and passes through the connected string. When passthrough is not connected, this editable text is returned.

passthrough.tooltip: Optional connected string to display and return unchanged.

frames.tooltip: MiniMax-H3 frame count at 24 fps. Valid values are 17*n+5 (5 to 362). Official range is 124-362 (5-15 s); shorter runs but is out-of-distribution.

CRT_MinimaxLength.name: CRT_MinimaxLength
CRT_MinimaxLength.description: Frame count snapped to MiniMax-H3's valid grid (17n+5, 24 fps, 5-15 s).

model.tooltip: The diffusion model to patch with the selected LoRA.

lora_folder.tooltip: Folder relative to models/loras, or an absolute folder. Only LoRA files directly inside it are considered.

seed.tooltip: Selects the LoRA by seed modulo sorted LoRA count. Use ComfyUI's fixed, increment, decrement, or randomize control.

strength_model.tooltip: Strength applied to the diffusion model.

PGC_SeededPersonaLoraLoader.name: PGC_SeededPersonaLoraLoader
PGC_SeededPersonaLoraLoader.description: Selects a LoRA deterministically from a folder using a native ComfyUI seed control, applies it to MODEL, and outputs its same-stem markdown persona as a string. Works with any model architecture.
output_tooltips: The model with the selected LoRA applied.
Contents of the .md file whose stem matches the selected LoRA.

fade_duration.tooltip: Fade duration in seconds for fade_loop mode

start_level.tooltip: Brightness at the very first frame.

mid_level.tooltip: Brightness at the exact center of the video.

end_level.tooltip: Brightness at the very last frame.

q_factor.tooltip: Curve Shape. 1.0=Linear, 2.0=Parabolic (Smooth). Higher values = Stays closer to Mid Level longer.

ReferenceLatentBatch.name: ReferenceLatentBatch
ReferenceLatentBatch.description: Accepts a batch of latent images and registers each frame as a separate reference, equivalent to chaining N ReferenceLatent nodes. Frames are sorted by full-content hash before registration so that any permutation of the same images produces byte-identical conditioning.

model_union_control.tooltip: Optional V2V Depth Control: model already merged with UnionControl / IC-LoRA guide support.

model_outpaint.tooltip: Optional V2V Outpaint mode model merged with IC-LoRA Outpaint.

model_upscale.tooltip: Optional V2V Upscale mode model merged with IC-LoRA Upscale.

spatial_upscale_model.tooltip: Optional latent upscaler used by HQ generation and V2V Upscale mode.

da3_model.tooltip: Depth Anything V3 model used to build V2V depth guides when no precomputed depth override is connected.

latent_downscale_factor.tooltip: Compression/downscale factor reported by the latent upscaler LoRA. Connect the loader output rather than guessing this value.

CRT_LTX23USModelsPipe.name: CRT_LTX23USModelsPipe
CRT_LTX23USModelsPipe.description: Bundles the LTX 2.3 model, video/audio VAEs, CLIP, and optional mode-specific models for the unified sampler.

Image I2V / V2V FirstFrame.tooltip: Starting image for I2V, or an optional first-frame anchor for V2V.

Video (V2V image batch).tooltip: Input video represented as an IMAGE batch. Required for V2V modes.

V2V Depth (override).tooltip: Optional precomputed depth guide for V2V Depth Control. When connected, skips DepthAnything inference.

source_audio.tooltip: Optional source audio used for conditioning and, when enabled, to derive the output frame count.

MegaPixels (override).tooltip: Values above 0 override the sampler megapixels_target; 0 keeps the sampler setting.

Frames (override).tooltip: Values above 0 override the sampler frame_count; 0 keeps the sampler setting.

Width T2V (override).tooltip: T2V width override. Use 0 to derive dimensions from megapixels and aspect ratio.

Height T2V (override).tooltip: T2V height override. Use 0 to derive dimensions from megapixels and aspect ratio.

HQ (override).tooltip: Config-pipe HQ override. When true it enables HQ even if the sampler widget is off.

CRT_LTX23USConfig.name: CRT_LTX23USConfig
CRT_LTX23USConfig.description: Collects the prompt, seed, optional image/video/audio inputs, and per-workflow overrides for the unified sampler.

workflow_mode.tooltip: Select image-to-video, text-to-video, or video-to-video execution. Required config inputs depend on this mode.

hq.tooltip: Generate directly at full resolution in one sampling pass for maximum quality. Disable HQ to use the faster two-stage path: half-resolution generation followed by latent upscale and refinement.

live_preview.tooltip: Decode intermediate previews during sampling. Useful for monitoring but adds decode overhead.

frame_count_from_audio.tooltip: When source audio is connected, derive the video length from its duration instead of frame_count.

vae_decode_tiled.tooltip: Decode video latents in tiles to reduce peak VRAM at the cost of additional processing time.

unload_model_before_vae_decode.tooltip: Unload the diffusion model after sampling and before VAE decode to reduce decode-time VRAM.

low_vram.tooltip: Unload CLIP after conditioning and VAEs before sampling, then reload VAEs for decode. Depth Anything V3 is always unloaded immediately after depth estimation.

megapixels_target.tooltip: Target output area in megapixels before model-specific dimension quantization.

frame_count.tooltip: Requested output length. LTX requires 8k+1 frames; invalid values are normalized automatically and reported in the console.

v2v_mode.tooltip: Depth Control follows scene depth; Outpaint expands the canvas; Upscale performs guided video enlargement. Each optional mode needs its matching model pipe input.

v2v_guide_strength.tooltip: Strength of the V2V depth guide. Higher values follow the source structure more closely.

depth_megapixels.tooltip: Resolution used only for DA3 depth estimation. DA3 is offloaded before the main V2V sampler starts.

steps.tooltip: Legacy compatibility value. LTX 2.3 distilled inference now always uses its fixed trained sigma schedule.

generated_audio_gain_db.tooltip: Gain applied to generated audio after decode, in decibels.

firstframe_strength.tooltip: Influence of the connected first-frame anchor. Zero disables anchoring; one applies full strength.

depth_cache_mode.tooltip: V2V Depth Control only. Disable reuse, keep the latest DA3 depth frames in RAM, or store them in ComfyUI's session temp directory. Temp files are cleared by ComfyUI at startup and graceful shutdown.

what_to_detect.tooltip: Text prompt used for subject detection, for example 'face' or 'person'.

performance_preset.tooltip: Fast = quickest detection, Balanced = default tradeoff, Quality = highest available quality in the current custom-node path and slower processing. The SAM path still uses a model-safe square working resolution.

single_item.tooltip: Limit detection to one item per frame. Enable this when you only want the main face/subject.

detect_chunk_size.tooltip: Detection batch size. 0 = process the whole batch at once, 1 = per-image processing, 2+ = fixed chunk size.

padding.tooltip: Extra border added around the input batch before detection so subjects near the edges are not cropped too tightly.

threshold.tooltip: Detection confidence threshold. Lower values find more masks, higher values are stricter.

bbox_expansion.tooltip: Expands the detected crop box around the subject. Higher values give a looser crop.

crop_smooth_alpha.tooltip: Temporal smoothing for crop position. Lower = steadier crop, higher = follows motion more closely.

crop_megapixels.tooltip: Target resolution for the cropped output images. 0 disables crop rescaling.

resize_back_to_original.tooltip: If disabled, upscale the original canvas to keep enhanced crop detail

what_to_detect.tooltip: Text prompt used by CLIPSeg, for example 'face' or 'person'.

performance_preset.tooltip: Fast = quickest detection, Balanced = default tradeoff, Quality = highest available quality in the current custom-node path and slower processing.

detect_chunk_size.tooltip: Detection batch size. 0 = process the whole batch at once, 1 = per-image processing, 2+ = fixed chunk size.

padding.tooltip: Extra border added around the input batch before detection so subjects near the edges are not cropped too tightly.

threshold.tooltip: Detection confidence threshold. Lower values find more mask areas, higher values are stricter.

blur_sigma.tooltip: Optional blur applied to CLIPSeg masks before crop extraction.

bbox_expansion.tooltip: Expands the detected crop box around the subject. Higher values give a looser crop.

crop_smooth_alpha.tooltip: Temporal smoothing for crop position. Lower = steadier crop, higher = follows motion more closely.

crop_megapixels.tooltip: Target resolution for the cropped output images. 0 disables crop rescaling.

Threshold.tooltip: Images with a rounded score strictly greater than this value are returned and optionally saved.

Path Save If above threshold.tooltip: Optional output folder for images above Threshold. Relative paths are resolved below ComfyUI/output; leave empty to disable saving.

attention_backend.tooltip: Attention implementation used when loading ERNIE. Auto prefers FlashAttention 2 when installed and compatible, otherwise eager attention.

keep_model_loaded.tooltip: Keep the model resident on the active device after scoring for faster subsequent runs at the cost of VRAM.

offload_to_cpu.tooltip: When keep_model_loaded is off, retain the cached model on CPU instead of releasing it completely. This reduces reload time but uses system RAM.

ErnieImageAestheticScore.name: ErnieImageAestheticScore
ErnieImageAestheticScore.description: Scores each input image from 0 to 100 with baidu/ERNIE-Image-Aes. Returns parallel INT and STRING lists in batch order, plus the highest-scoring image and the batch scoring above Threshold. The model downloads on first use.

image.tooltip: Optional image batch. The model loaded in Unsloth Studio must support vision input.

unsloth_server_url.tooltip: Leave the default to discover Studio's active local llama-server port from its logs. Enter a reachable non-default llama-server base URL to bypass discovery. Studio must have a model loaded; image input requires a vision-capable model.

skills_path.tooltip: Optional directory with skill files. Every .md file in the folder and its subfolders is loaded recursively and appended to the system prompt as extra context.

disable_thinking.tooltip: Request a direct answer by disabling supported model thinking mode. Models that ignore this chat-template option are unaffected.

include_reasoning.tooltip: Append reasoning_content returned by the server to the response output when the loaded model provides it.

reuse_context.tooltip: Keep the system prompt and skill files in the llama-server slot cache between runs: only the new user content (image + prompt) is evaluated, making repeated runs much faster. Editing the system prompt or a skill file changes the prefix and automatically rebuilds the cache once.

clear_prompt_cache.tooltip: Erase llama-server slot 0 after generation, forcing the next run to reprocess the full prompt. Leave off to keep context reuse.

UnslothLLM.name: UnslothLLM
UnslothLLM.description: Connects ComfyUI to the model currently loaded in Unsloth Studio. Unsloth Studio must remain open; image input requires a vision model.

keep_blocks.tooltip: Comma-separated block indexes to keep in the saved LoRA. Empty = save all blocks. Supports ranges like 0-13,16,17,26,27.

rank.tooltip: SVD rank for compression. 0 = lossless diff format (larger file). >0 = LoRA format with SVD at this rank.

enable_translation.tooltip: Translate the Whisper transcript with the optional local llama.cpp runtime. Requires a separately installed llama-cpp-python package.

translation_language.tooltip: Target language used when translation is enabled and for translated OmniVoice output.

CreateFadeMaskAdvanced.name: CreateFadeMaskAdvanced
CreateFadeMaskAdvanced.description:
Create a batch of masks interpolated between given frames and values. 
Uses same syntax as Fizz' BatchValueSchedule.
First value is the frame index (not that this starts from 0, not 1) 
and the second value inside the brackets is the float value of the mask in range 0.0 - 1.0  

For example the default values:  
0:(0.0)  
7:(1.0)  
15:(0.0)  
  
Would create a mask batch fo 16 frames, starting from black, 
interpolating with the chosen curve to fully white at the 8th frame, 
and interpolating from that to fully black at the 16th frame.

ColorMatch.name: ColorMatch
ColorMatch.description:
color-matcher enables color transfer across images which comes in handy for automatic  
color-grading of photographs, paintings and film sequences as well as light-field  
and stopmotion corrections.  

The methods behind the mappings are based on the approach from Reinhard et al.,  
the Monge-Kantorovich Linearization (MKL) as proposed by Pitie et al. and our analytical solution  
to a Multi-Variate Gaussian Distribution (MVGD) transfer in conjunction with classical histogram   
matching. As shown below our HM-MVGD-HM compound outperforms existing methods.   
https://github.com/hahnec/color-matcher/

the Monge-Kantorovich Linearization (MKL) as proposed by Pitie et al. and our analytical solution  
to a Multi-Variate Gaussian Distribution (MVGD) transfer in conjunction with classical histogram   
matching. As shown below our HM-MVGD-HM compound outperforms existing methods.   
https://github.com/hahnec/color-matcher/   

'reinhard_lab_gpu' method uses Kornia for GPU-accelerated color transfer in Lab color space.

ImageTransformKJ.name: ImageTransformKJ
ImageTransformKJ.description:
Interactive image transform node: crop, resize, pad, and rotate.  
Connect an image input — the preview appears automatically.  

Cropping:  
Click + drag to draw a crop region.  
Drag inside to move, drag edges/corners to resize.  
Right-click to delete a region.  
Ctrl to snap to grid.  
Shift + resize to constrain aspect ratio.  
Alt + resize to resize symmetrically.  

Padding:  
Shift + drag to adjust padding position.

Rotate button enables rotation cross (drag to rotate, right-click to reset).  
Set target_width/height to resize output (0 = keep original).  
Use keep_proportion to control how the image fits the target.  
Use extra_padding to add padding with color or edge fill (clamp/repeat/mirror).

Visual prompt builder for Ideogram 4's structured JSON caption format.

Drag on the canvas to draw regions; select a region to set its type (obj/text),  
description, text, and color palette. Set the background and optional style fields  
as widgets. Outputs the assembled caption JSON string.  

bbox is normalized to a 0-1000 grid as [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax]; width/height set
the canvas aspect ratio.

Canvas controls:
- Drag: draw a new region
- Ctrl/Cmd-drag: force-draw a new region even on top of an existing one
- Click: select a region · Alt-click: cycle overlapping regions
- Double-click: edit the description inline
- Right-click: region list (select / delete / duplicate / reorder, top = front)
- Del / Backspace: remove the selected region
- Ctrl/Cmd + C / V / D: copy / paste / duplicate the selected region

Color swatches:
- Click: edit · Drag: reorder · Right-click: remove
- Hover + Ctrl/Cmd + C / V: copy / paste the hex
- "+": add a color (uses the clipboard color if it is one)

Toolbar:

- Grab BG / Clear BG: use the last generated image as the background
- brightness slider, token estimate, and Copy / Paste / Clear all

HDRPreviewKJ.name: HDRPreviewKJ
HDRPreviewKJ.description:
Realtime-exposure preview for HDR-compressed images.

Input: LogC3-compressed [0,1] image/video batch (e.g. the VAE-decoded output of an HDR IC-LoRA workflow, prior to HDR decompression).

Decompression + exposure + saturation + Reinhard tonemap + sRGB runs in a WebGL fragment shader in the browser for realtime slider feedback, and the same math runs server-side to produce the baked sRGB IMAGE output. Slider changes update the preview immediately; the IMAGE output only updates when the workflow is re-queued.

ImageSharpenKJ.name: ImageSharpenKJ
ImageSharpenKJ.description:
GPU-accelerated image sharpening with multiple methods.

**RCAS** — AMD's Robust Contrast-Adaptive Sharpening (from FSR).
Single 5-tap cross filter that adapts to local contrast.
Minimal artifacts, good for general use with little tuning.

**Adaptive USM** — Unsharp mask with local variance modulation.
Sharpens detail-rich areas more, flat/noisy areas less.
More controllable than RCAS via radius and threshold parameters.

**High-Pass** — Extracts high-frequency detail and blends it back.
Gives a "clarity" enhancement feel. Uses radius to control detail scale.

**Deconvolution** — Richardson-Lucy iterative deconvolution.
Can recover actual lost detail from blur, not just enhance edges.
Uses radius as the estimated blur kernel and iterations to control convergence.

SplineEditor.name: SplineEditor
SplineEditor.description:
# WORK IN PROGRESS  
Do not count on this as part of your workflow yet,  
probably contains lots of bugs and stability is not  
guaranteed!!  
  
## Graphical editor to create values for various   
## schedules and/or mask batches.  

**Shift + click** to add control point at end.
**Ctrl + click** to add control point (subdivide) between two points.  
**Right click on a point** to delete it.    
Note that you can't delete from start/end.  
  
Right click on canvas for context menu:  
NEW!:
- Add new spline
    - Creates a new spline on same canvas, currently these paths are only outputed  
      as coordinates.
- Add single point
    - Creates a single point that only returns it's current position coords  
- Delete spline
    - Deletes the currently selected spline, you can select a spline by clicking on   
    it's path, or cycle through them with the 'Next spline' -option.  

These are purely visual options, doesn't affect the output:  
 - Toggle handles visibility
 - Display sample points: display the points to be returned.  

**points_to_sample** value sets the number of samples  
returned from the **drawn spline itself**, this is independent from the  
actual control points, so the interpolation type matters.  
sampling_method: 
 - time: samples along the time axis, used for schedules  
 - path: samples along the path itself, useful for coordinates  
 - controlpoints: samples only the control points themselves  

output types:
 - mask batch  
        example compatible nodes: anything that takes masks  
 - list of floats
        example compatible nodes: IPAdapter weights  
 - pandas series
        example compatible nodes: anything that takes Fizz'  
        nodes Batch Value Schedule  
 - torch tensor  
        example compatible nodes: unknown

GLIGENTextBoxApplyBatchCoords.description:
This node allows scheduling GLIGEN text box positions in a batch,  
to be used with AnimateDiff-Evolved. Intended to pair with the  
Spline Editor -node.  

GLIGEN model can be downloaded through the Manage's "Install Models" menu.  
Or directly from here:  
https://huggingface.co/comfyanonymous/GLIGEN_pruned_safetensors/tree/main  
  
Inputs:  
- **latents** input is used to calculate batch size  
- **clip** is your standard text encoder, use same as for the main prompt  
- **gligen_textbox_model** connects to GLIGEN Loader  
- **coordinates** takes a json string of points, directly compatible  
with the spline editor node.
- **text** is the part of the prompt to set position for  
- **width** and **height** are the size of the GLIGEN bounding box  
  
Outputs:
- **conditioning** goes between to clip text encode and the sampler  
- **coord_preview** is an optional preview of the coordinates and  
bounding boxes.

closed_loop.tooltip: Wrap looped-schedule windows around the end back to frame 0.

causal_window_fix.tooltip: Prepend an anchor frame to non-0 windows, stripped after the model call.

freenoise.tooltip: FreeNoise noise shuffling for smoother blending. Model path only.

cond_retain_index_list.tooltip: Comma-separated window-relative indices that keep their original conditioning, e.g. '0' reuses the start frame's cond per window. No viz effect; model path only.

model.tooltip: Optional model to apply the context windows to during sampling.

output_tooltips: Model with context windows applied; only valid when a model is connected.
ContextWindowsVisualizerKJ.name: ContextWindowsVisualizerKJ
ContextWindowsVisualizerKJ.description: Interactive visualization of ComfyUI context windows: window placement, overlap, fuse weights and per-frame blending, updated live. Optionally applies the settings to a model like the core Context Windows (Manual) node.

patch_order.tooltip: Patch the comfy patch_model function to load weight patches (LoRAs) before compiling the model

full_load.tooltip: Disabling may help with memory issues when loading large models, when changing this you should probably force model reload to avoid issues!

PatchModelPatcherOrder.name: PatchModelPatcherOrder
PatchModelPatcherOrder.description: NO LONGER NECESSARY OR FUNCTIONAL, keeping node for backwards compatibility. Use the TorchCompileModelAdvanced to use LoRA with torch.compile.

TorchCompileModelFluxAdvanced.name: TorchCompileModelFluxAdvanced
TorchCompileModelFluxAdvanced.description: This node has been replaced with TorchCompileModelAdvanced node, please use that instead.

TorchCompileLTXModel.name: TorchCompileLTXModel
TorchCompileLTXModel.description: This node has been replaced with TorchCompileModelAdvanced node, please use that instead.

TorchCompileCosmosModel.name: TorchCompileCosmosModel
TorchCompileCosmosModel.description: This node has been replaced with TorchCompileModelAdvanced node, please use that instead.

TorchCompileModelHyVideo.name: TorchCompileModelHyVideo
TorchCompileModelHyVideo.description: This node has been replaced with TorchCompileModelAdvanced node, please use that instead.

TorchCompileModelQwenImage.name: TorchCompileModelQwenImage
TorchCompileModelQwenImage.description: This node has been replaced with TorchCompileModelAdvanced node, please use that instead.

TorchCompileModelWanVideo.name: TorchCompileModelWanVideo
TorchCompileModelWanVideo.description: This node has been replaced with TorchCompileModelAdvanced node, please use that instead.

latent.tooltip: Only used to get the latent count

positive.tooltip: Positive conditioning to which guide keyframe info will be added

negative.tooltip: Negative conditioning to which guide keyframe info will be added

vae.tooltip: Video VAE used to encode the guide images

latent.tooltip: Video latent, guides are added to the end of this latent

num_guides.tooltip: Select how many guide images to use

output_tooltips: Video latent with added guides
LTXVAddGuideMulti.name: LTXVAddGuideMulti
LTXVAddGuideMulti.description: Add multiple guide images at specified frame indices with strengths, uses DynamicCombo which requires ComfyUI 0.8.1 and frontend 1.33.4 or later.

images.tooltip: Batch of images - non-black images will be used as guides

strength.tooltip: Strength for all guides.

LTXVAddGuidesFromBatch.name: LTXVAddGuidesFromBatch
LTXVAddGuidesFromBatch.description: Adds multiple guide images from a batch to the latent at corresponding frame indices. Non-black images in the batch are used as guides.

video_start_time.tooltip: Start time in seconds for the video mask.

video_end_time.tooltip: End time in seconds for the video mask.

audio_start_time.tooltip: Start time in seconds for the audio mask.

audio_end_time.tooltip: End time in seconds for the audio mask.

max_length.tooltip: 'truncate': cut latent to end_time length. 'pad': extend latent to end_time. 'partial': mask range within existing latent.

existing_mask_mode.tooltip: How to combine with existing noise masks if present. 'add' will take the max of existing and new mask, 'overwrite' will replace with new mask. 'subtract' will set the masked region to 0 instead of 1, effectively unmasking it.

LTXVAudioVideoMask.name: LTXVAudioVideoMask
LTXVAudioVideoMask.description: Creates noise masks for video and audio latents based on specified time ranges. New content is generated within these masked regions

nag_alpha.tooltip: Mixing coefficient in that controls the balance between the normalized guided representation and the original positive representation.

nag_tau.tooltip: Clipping threshold that controls how much the guided attention can deviate from the positive attention.

inplace.tooltip: If true, modifies tensors in place to save memory. Leads to different numerical results which may change the output slightly.

chunks.tooltip: Number of chunks to split the feedforward activations into to reduce peak VRAM usage.

dim_threshold.tooltip: Dimension threshold above which to apply chunking.

LTXVChunkFeedForward.name: LTXVChunkFeedForward
LTXVChunkFeedForward.description: EXPERIMENTAL AND MAY CHANGE THE MODEL OUTPUT!! Chunks feedforward activations to reduce peak VRAM usage.

model.tooltip: The model to add preview override to.

latent_upscale_model.tooltip: Optional upscale model to use for higher resolution previews.

vae.tooltip: VAE model to use normalizing the latents for the upscale model.

output_tooltips: The model with Sampling Preview Override.
LTX2SamplingPreviewOverride.name: LTX2SamplingPreviewOverride
LTX2SamplingPreviewOverride.description: Overrides the LTX2 preview sampling preview function, temporary measure until previews are in comfy core

model.tooltip: The model to add preview override to.

audio_normalization_factors.tooltip: Comma-separated list of audio normalization factors to apply at each sampling step. For example, '1,1,0.25,1,1,0.25,1,1' will apply a factor of 0.25 at the 3rd and 6th steps.

output_tooltips: The model with Audio Latent Normalizing Sampling.
LTX2AudioLatentNormalizingSampling.name: LTX2AudioLatentNormalizingSampling
LTX2AudioLatentNormalizingSampling.description: Improves LTX2 generated audio quality by normalizing audio latents at specified sampling steps.

MiniMaxChunkFeedForward.name: MiniMaxChunkFeedForward
MiniMaxChunkFeedForward.description: Chunks the MiniMax H3 feedforward (SwiGLU) over the packed token dim to reduce peak VRAM usage. Each chunk still goes through ComfyUI's fused INT8 kernel when the model is quantized, and since activations are quantized per-token the output matches the unchunked model.

head_chunks.tooltip: Number of head groups to split the attention call into. Kernel-internal transients scale down with this; heads are independent so the result is unchanged.

MiniMaxLowVRAMAttention.name: MiniMaxLowVRAMAttention
MiniMaxLowVRAMAttention.description: Reduces peak VRAM of the MiniMax H3 attention without changing the math. Splits the attention call into head groups so the kernel's internal transients (int8 q/k copies, fp32 accumulator) shrink by the chunk count while the fused qkv buffer is alive, and frees the qkv buffer / normed block input as soon as they're consumed. Output is identical to the unpatched model.

fuse_norm_silu.tooltip: Replace norm+SiLU chains (RMSNorm for Wan, GroupNorm for KL VAEs) with fused Triton kernels (single pass, fp32 accumulation). Requires triton.

channels_last.tooltip: Convert conv weights to channels_last memory format, removing cuDNN layout transposes around every conv. Required for the fused GroupNorm kernel to engage on KL VAEs.

int8_conv.tooltip: EXPERIMENTAL: run the VAE decoder's 3x3 convolutions on int8 tensor cores (4x the bf16 rate on Ada+). Weights quantized per-out-channel, activations dynamically per-tensor; ~45-48 dB vs the bf16 decode, minor quality loss possible. Wan 2.1/2.2 and KL image VAEs (Flux2/SDXL/SD1.5), ignored for others.

autotune.tooltip: Benchmark several kernel block-size configs on first use of each tensor shape and cache the fastest. Brief stutter per new resolution, usually a few percent faster after warmup.

PatchTritonVAE.name: PatchTritonVAE
PatchTritonVAE.description: Speeds up VAE decode/encode with fused Triton norm+SiLU kernels and channels_last conv layout. Supported VAEs (auto-detected): Wan 2.1/2.2 video VAEs incl. Qwen-Image (RMSNorm, ~1.4x/1.15x), KL image VAEs such as Flux/Flux2, SDXL and SD1.5 (GroupNorm, ~1.6-1.8x at 2048px), and LTXV/LTX2 video VAEs (PixelNorm; timestep-conditioned decoder blocks get norm-only fusion). Other architectures are not supported. Applied as object patches on a cloned patcher, so it only exists while this VAE is loaded.

context_length.tooltip: Frames of the previous clip's picture to carry over. Only these lengths are whole numbers of latent steps, so only these are offered. 5 is just barely fluid, 22 is nearly seamless. Longer windows pin more motion but come off the front of the delivered clip, so 56 spends 2.3 seconds of the render on frames you throw away.

audio_context_length.tooltip: Frames of tail audio to pin, independent of the picture window. 0 follows it. The window is END-aligned with the pinned video, so this only controls how far back the sound reaches. Multiples of 3 land exactly on the 40 Hz audio grid and multiples of 24 are whole seconds: 24 pins the last second. Off-grid values are widened to the nearest whole step.

context_frames.tooltip: Decoded frames of the previous clip. Used when no context_latent is wired. When one is, the picture comes from it instead and this is ignored.

context_latent.tooltip: Previous clip's SAMPLER OUTPUT latent (the same one you wire into the decode nodes). Supplies both picture and sound, sliced straight out, skipping the decode and re-encode that cost a little quality at every link of a chain. Must be the same resolution as the clip being generated.

audio_vae.tooltip: H3 audio VAE. Supply with context_audio to carry the previous clip's tail sound across the join. Not needed when context_latent is wired.

context_audio.tooltip: Audio of the previous clip. The tail matching the pinned frames is encoded and pinned alongside them. Ignored when context_latent is wired.

MiniMaxH3MotionContext.name: MiniMaxH3MotionContext
MiniMaxH3MotionContext.description: Pin a run of consecutive frames from a previous clip as never-denoised conditioning rows, so the model reads real motion instead of guessing it from a single still. With context_latent wired, both picture and sound are sliced from the previous clip's latent, skipping the decode and re-encode that cost a little quality at every link. A last_frame anchor on the incoming conditioning is kept and pinned alongside the head.

audio.tooltip: Decoded audio for the same clip. Trimmed by the matching duration so sound stays locked to picture. Leave unwired for silent clips.

fps.tooltip: Frame rate used to convert the trim into an audio duration. Must match what you feed Create Video.

match_tail.tooltip: Make the audio duration equal frames/fps exactly, trimming a long tail or padding a short one with silence. H3 rounds its audio grid to the nearest step, so each clip carries about 8ms too much or too little sound, which accumulates at every join in a chain.

MiniMaxH3MotionContextTrim.name: MiniMaxH3MotionContextTrim
MiniMaxH3MotionContextTrim.description: Remove the leading pinned frames from a decoded H3 clip, trimming picture and sound by the same duration.

latent.tooltip: The sampler's output latent (the same one you wire into the decode nodes).

filename_prefix.tooltip: Saved under the ComfyUI output folder. The default keeps all chain latents in one folder so the Load node can always pick the newest.

clip_index.tooltip: Which clip of the chain THIS is. Saves to that clip's fixed slot, so a re-roll overwrites its own reject instead of stacking new files. First clip: 1 here and 0 on the Load node. Clip 2: 2 here and 1 on the Load node. 0 = old behaviour, a new numbered file every run (numbers count runs, not clips).

This node is a specialized detailer node for enhancing video details, such as in AnimateDiff. It can handle cases where the masks contained in SEGS serve as batch masks spanning multiple frames.

sam_model.tooltip:
Segment Anything Model for Silhouette Detection.
Be sure to use the SAM_MODEL loaded through the SAMLoader (Impact) node as input.

segs.tooltip:
This is the segment information detected by the detector.
It refines the Mask through the SAM (Segment Anything) detector for all areas pointed to by SEGS, and combines all Masks to return as a single Mask.

image.tooltip: It is assumed that segs contains only the information about the detected areas, and does not include the image. SAM (Segment Anything) operates by referencing this image.

detection_hint.tooltip:
It is recommended to use only center-1.
When refining the mask of SEGS with the SAM (Segment Anything) model, center-1 uses only the rectangular area of SEGS and a single point at the exact center as hints.
Other options were added during the experimental stage and do not work well.

dilation.tooltip: Set the value to dilate the result mask. If the value is negative, it erodes the mask.

threshold.tooltip: Set the sensitivity threshold for the mask detected by SAM (Segment Anything). A higher value generates a more specific mask with a narrower range. For example, when pointing to a person's area, it might detect clothes, which is a narrower range, instead of the entire person.

bbox_expansion.tooltip: When performing SAM (Segment Anything) detection within the SEGS area, the rectangular area of SEGS is expanded and used as a hint.

mask_hint_threshold.tooltip:
When detection_hint is mask-area, the mask of SEGS is used as a point hint for SAM (Segment Anything).
In this case, only the areas of the mask with brightness values equal to or greater than mask_hint_threshold are used as hints.

mask_hint_use_negative.tooltip:
When detecting with SAM (Segment Anything), negative hints are applied as follows:
Small: When the SEGS is smaller than 10 pixels in size
Outer: Sampling the image area outside the SEGS region at regular intervals

FaceDetailer.description:
This node enhances details by automatically detecting specific objects in the input image using detection models (bbox, segm, sam) and regenerating the image by enlarging the detected area based on the guide size.
Although this node is specialized to simplify the commonly used facial detail enhancement workflow, it can also be used for various automatic inpainting purposes depending on the detection model.

ImpactWildcardProcessor.name: ImpactWildcardProcessor
ImpactWildcardProcessor.description:
The 'ImpactWildcardProcessor' processes text prompts written in wildcard syntax and outputs the processed text prompt.

TIP: Before the workflow is executed, the processing result of 'wildcard_text' is displayed in 'populated_text', and the populated text is saved along with the workflow. If you want to use a seed converted as input, write the prompt directly in 'populated_text' instead of 'wildcard_text', and set the mode to 'fixed'.

ImpactWildcardEncode.name: ImpactWildcardEncode
ImpactWildcardEncode.description:
The 'ImpactWildcardEncode' node processes text prompts written in wildcard syntax and outputs them as conditioning. It also supports LoRA syntax, with the applied LoRA reflected in the model's output.

TIP1: Before the workflow is executed, the processing result of 'wildcard_text' is displayed in 'populated_text', and the populated text is saved along with the workflow. If you want to use a seed converted as input, write the prompt directly in 'populated_text' instead of 'wildcard_text', and set the mode to 'fixed'.
TIP2: If the 'Inspire Pack' is installed, LBW(LoRA Block Weight) syntax can also be applied.

seed_2nd.tooltip: Additional noise seed. The behavior is determined by seed_2nd_mode.

seed_2nd_mode.tooltip: application method of seed_2nd. 1) ignore: Do not use seed_2nd. In the base only sampling stage, the seed is applied as a noise seed, and in the regional sampling stage, denoising is performed as it is without additional noise. 2) Others: In the base only sampling stage, the seed is applied as a noise seed, and once it is closed so that there is no leftover noise, new noise is added with seed_2nd and the regional samping stage is performed. a) fixed: Use seed_2nd as it is as an additional noise seed. b) seed+seed_2nd: Apply the value of seed+seed_2nd as an additional noise seed. c) seed-seed_2nd: Apply the value of seed-seed_2nd as an additional noise seed. d) increment: Not implemented yet. Same with fixed. e) decrement: Not implemented yet. Same with fixed. f) randomize: Not implemented yet. Same with fixed.
